I added `withoutHost` to the end of `src/utils.ts`. Nothing else in the file changed. The type check reports no errors, and the existing suite still passes (13 files, 424 tests). It is exported from the package through the existing `export * from "./utils"` in `src/index.ts`.

The signature is `export function withoutHost(input: string)`, exactly as the ticket wrote it, with no return type. The spec explicitly rejected adding `: string`. That has one side effect on this stub: a function declaration whose body only throws gets `void` as its inferred return type, so the spec's type test (`expectTypeOf(withoutHost("")).toEqualTypeOf<string>()`) fails against the stub. It will pass once the real body returns a string. The doc comment states that the result is a string (`pathname + search + hash`, with `"/"` when the path is empty) and that the function never throws for a string input.

Added exports: `withoutHost`

public.finalText:
I wrote the test suite in `test/ufo-without-host-check.test.ts`. It has two tests for each of the spec's 18 scenarios: the happy path and one boundary case. That covers happy 1–5, boundary 1–10 and unhappy 1–3, as flat `test(...)` calls named `[kind-N] …`.

- **Type check:** `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors. That `tsconfig.json` only includes `src`, so the test file isn't type-checked by that command.
- **Against the stub:** `npx vitest run test/ufo-without-host-check.` fails all 36 tests, as expected, because `withoutHost` still throws.
- **Expected values checked:** the spec defines the result as `(pathname || "/") + search + hash` from `parseURL`. I ran all 36 tests against a throwaway copy that used that formula instead of the real import, and all passed. I then deleted that copy, along with an earlier one-off file that printed `parseURL` output for the boundary inputs.
- **Boundary cases beyond the spec:** where a scenario has only one example, I picked inputs like `"\n  https://a.com"`, `"HTTPS:\\\\a.com\\x\\y"`, `"//u@example.com:80/a"` and `"mailto:"`. Their expected values come from the spec's rule plus what the unchanged `parseURL` returns today.
- **Left out:** I didn't add the `expectTypeOf(withoutHost("")).toEqualTypeOf<string>()` check. It isn't one of the scenarios, and while the body throws, the inferred return type is `never`, so that check would fail.

Nothing else in the repository was changed.

36 tests, in 1 file.

private.finalText:
I wrote the hidden suite in `test/hidden-ufo-without-host-check/without-host.test.ts`. All 60 tests fail against the current stub, which throws `not implemented`. Before that, I ran a temporary copy against the spec's own formula, `(pathname || "/") + search + hash` from `parseURL`, and all 60 passed; the copy has been deleted. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors, and nothing outside the test folder changed.

**Type check.** That config only checks `src`. When I type-checked my file directly, one error remained: the `expectTypeOf(...).toEqualTypeOf<string>()` line in `[happy-1]`. That is the spec's type test, and it fails because the stub's return type is currently inferred as `void`. It will pass once the function returns a string.

**Coverage.** Every scenario has a test that checks its exact table rows: happy-1 to happy-5, boundary-1 to boundary-10, and unhappy-1 to unhappy-3. Each public test has at least one test that extends it, named in a comment above. The tests aimed at shortcuts that pass the public suite but not the spec:
- **Greedy host stripping:** a URL inside the query, such as `http://a.com?q=http://b.com/x`, must give `/?q=http://b.com/x`.
- **Treating `@` as the end of the login part:** `http://a.com/x@y` must give `/x@y`.
- **Protocols without `//`:** `mailto:a@b.com?subject=x#h` gives `/`, so the query and fragment are dropped too. The same applies to `ab:/y`, `localhost:3000/api?x=1` and `a.com:8080/x`, which `parseURL` reads as having a protocol.
- **Special protocols:** `blob:https://a.com/uuid` keeps `https://a.com/uuid`, `data:text/html?x#y` keeps `text/html?x#y`, and a bare `javascript:` gives `/`.
- **Rules that only apply to inputs with a protocol:**
  - In a full URL, backslashes become `/` even in the query and fragment.
  - In a plain path, backslashes and leading spaces are kept: `foo\bar`, `  /foo`, `  ?x` and `  //a.com/x` come back unchanged, with no `/` added.
- **Drive letters:** `parseURL` turns `file:///C:/x/y` into `C:/x/y`.
- **Decoding:** bad percent sequences such as `%zz` are kept and nothing throws.
- **Cross-check:** one test compares the result with `parseURL` over 12 mixed inputs.

60 tests, in 1 file.

Open in the spec: none
